newsitem.title: UK: NWE cracked fuel oils firmer, HS barges trade $3 up.
newsitem.headline: NWE cracked fuel oils firmer, HS barges trade $3 up.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil prices were mostly firmer in line with crude on Wednesday, but high sulphur barges continued to get extra lift from cargo pricing, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded up to $91 a tonne fob refinery Rotterdam helped one trader's cargo pricing strategy, but prices drifted off the high with buying interest otherwise thin.
Rotterdam barges were later talked around $188/$190 a tonne fob while Antwerp liftings talked $88.50/$89 with several players seen long of product at the port.
High sulphur cargoes firmed around $3 per tonne to value around $88 cif NWE but trade was thin with little fresh demand from end-users at these higher levels.
Traders said firm prices for fob stems in NWE continued to limit arbitrage options into the Mediterranean market where recent Eastern arbitrage has drawn on supplies.

The low sulphur barge and cargo markets remained in the doldrums. Outright prices strengthened with crude but the high/low sulphur spread widened with low sulphur's rise limited by slack buying interest.
